title: Interactive element without a meaningful name
user_impact: Screen reader users are not told what the element does.
technical_impact: An element whose role requires a name (such as checkbox, combobox, listbox, radio, slider, switch, tab, textbox, menu item, image role, or a form field whose label is empty) has no accessible name from aria-label, aria-labelledby, a label or its content, so a screen reader announces only the role; buttons, links, dialogs, <summary> and fields without any label have their own rules.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content for the img role (ACT 23a2a8 Image has non-empty accessible name; F65, ARIA6, ARIA10); WAI-ARIA 1.2 (Accessible Name Required: True); accname 1.2
checks.applicability: Elements in the accessibility tree whose role requires a name (checkbox, combobox, listbox, menuitem*, meter, option, progressbar, radio, radiogroup, searchbox, slider, spinbutton, switch, tab, textbox, tree, treeitem, ...), except a[href] (links/name-missing), buttons (buttons/name-missing), dialogs (dialog/name-missing) and native fields with no label source at all (forms/label-missing). For the img role: HTML elements that become an image through role="img" (ACT 23a2a8); itself is images/alt-missing,
checks.expectation:
Fails when the computed name is empty: a custom slider without label, a switch whose
aria-labelledby points at empty text, a native field whose <label> is blank, a listbox or tree
without name, an element with role="img" without a name. An empty aria-label is no name and
does not mark an image decorative (only role none/presentation or aria-hidden do), and an image
inside a named link or button is no exception (ACT 23a2a8 has none). Every name source passes:
aria-label, aria-labelledby, <label>, title on a native field, content for name-from-content
roles. Hidden subtrees are out of scope. The report files the finding under 4.1.2, the one
criterion of this id, also for the img role, whose finding a11y-rules tags 1.1.1.
